# US-China Trade War: Tariffs, Trade Volumes, and Supply Chain Shifts (2016–2024)

## Overview
This collection of datasets tracks the evolution of the US-China trade war from 2016 to 2024, covering tariff rate changes, bilateral trade volumes, supply chain diversification patterns, and key policy milestones.

## Data Source

### tariff_rates
Average effective tariff rates by half-year period (2017-H1 to 2024-H1). Fields: `period` (string, format YYYY-HX), `us_tariff_on_china` (percent, range 3.1–25.4), `china_tariff_on_us` (percent, range 8.0–23.1). Rates represent trade-weighted averages across all tariff lines.

### bilateral_trade
Annual US-China bilateral trade from 2016 to 2024. Fields: `year` (integer), `us_exports_to_china` (billion USD), `us_imports_from_china` (billion USD), `total_bilateral` (billion USD, sum of exports and imports).

### supply_chain_share
Annual share of total US goods imports by source. Fields: `year` (integer), `china` (percent), `vietnam` (percent), `india` (percent), `rest_of_world` (percent). Values for each year sum to approximately 100%.

### policy_events
Key policy milestones. Fields: `date` (ISO date string), `period_approx` (corresponding half-year period), `event` (short description), `category` (one of: investigation, tariff, deal, review). Contains 12 events spanning August 2017 to May 2024.

## Data Notes
- Tariff rates are approximate trade-weighted averages and may differ from statutory rates on specific product categories
- 2024 data is partial (H1 only for tariffs; full-year trade figures are estimates)
- Supply chain shares are rounded and may not sum to exactly 100%
- Rest-of-world is a residual category capturing all non-China, non-Vietnam, non-India imports

This collection of datasets tracks the evolution of the US-China trade war from 2016 to 2024, covering tariff rate changes, bilateral trade volumes, supply chain diversification patterns, and key policy milestones.

## Data Notes

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
from datetime import datetime
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# ── Data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
tariff_periods = ["2017\nH1","2017\nH2","2018\nH1","2018\nH2","2019\nH1","2019\nH2",
                  "2020\nH1","2020\nH2","2021\nH1","2021\nH2","2022\nH1","2022\nH2",
                  "2023\nH1","2023\nH2","2024\nH1"]
us_tariff    = [3.1, 3.1, 3.8, 12.0, 18.3, 21.0, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 25.4]
china_tariff = [8.0, 8.0, 8.0, 16.5, 20.7, 21.8, 20.9, 20.9, 20.9, 20.9, 21.1, 21.1, 21.2, 21.2, 23.1]

years_annual = np.array([2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024])
us_exports   = np.array([115.6, 129.9, 120.3, 106.4, 124.5, 151.1, 153.8, 147.8, 138.2])
us_imports   = np.array([462.6, 505.5, 539.5, 452.2, 435.4, 506.4, 536.8, 427.2, 401.5])
total_bilat  = np.array([578.2, 635.4, 659.8, 558.6, 559.9, 657.5, 690.6, 575.0, 539.7])

china_sc   = [21.4, 21.6, 21.2, 18.1, 18.6, 17.9, 16.5, 13.9, 12.8]
vietnam_sc = [2.1, 2.2, 2.6, 2.9, 3.4, 3.7, 3.9, 4.5, 4.9]
india_sc   = [2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.3, 2.7, 2.8, 3.1, 3.4]

# Policy events — simplified labels
events_data = [
    ("2017-08-14", "Section 301\nInvestigation\ninitiated", "investigation"),
    ("2018-07-06", "List 1: 25% on\n$34B goods", "tariff"),
    ("2018-09-24", "List 3: 10% on\n$200B goods", "tariff"),
    ("2019-05-10", "List 3 raised\nto 25%", "tariff"),
    ("2019-09-01", "List 4A: 15% on\n$112B goods", "tariff"),
    ("2020-01-15", "Phase One\nDeal Signed", "deal"),
    ("2021-10-04", "USTR tariff\nreview framework", "review"),
    ("2022-06-20", "Selective tariff\nexclusions review", "review"),
    ("2024-05-14", "Biden: EVs 100%,\nsemiconductors 50%", "tariff"),
]

# ── Color palette ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C_US     = "#1b3a5c"
C_CN     = "#c44e52"
C_VN     = "#dd8452"
C_IN     = "#55a868"
C_GRID   = "#d8d8d8"
C_BG     = "#fcfcfc"
C_TARIFF_EVENT = "#c44e52"
C_INVESTIGATION = "#8e6aaf"
C_DEAL   = "#3a9a5c"
C_REVIEW = "#4c9eb5"
C_BAR_EXPORT = "#3b6da8"
C_BAR_IMPORT = "#c44e52"

def date_to_idx(d):
    ref = datetime(2017, 1, 1)
    tgt = datetime.strptime(d, "%Y-%m-%d")
    days = (tgt - ref).days
    half_years = days / 182.625
    return half_years

# ── Figure ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "font.size": 9,
    "axes.titlesize": 11.5,
    "axes.labelsize": 9.5,
    "axes.linewidth": 0.6,
    "xtick.labelsize": 7.5,
    "ytick.labelsize": 7.5,
    "legend.fontsize": 7,
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.facecolor": C_BG,
    "grid.alpha": 0.35,
})

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12.5, 14.5), dpi=200)
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 1, hspace=0.5, left=0.09, right=0.94, top=0.93, bottom=0.04)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PANEL A: Tariff Escalation with Policy Events
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0])
x_t = np.arange(len(tariff_periods))

# Fill between to highlight escalation gap
ax1.fill_between(x_t, us_tariff, china_tariff, where=np.array(china_tariff) >= np.array(us_tariff),
                 color=C_CN, alpha=0.06, zorder=1)
ax1.fill_between(x_t, china_tariff, us_tariff, where=np.array(us_tariff) > np.array(china_tariff),
                 color=C_US, alpha=0.06, zorder=1)

# Tariff lines
ax1.plot(x_t, us_tariff, color=C_US, linewidth=2.0, marker="o", markersize=4.5,
         markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.5, markeredgecolor=C_US,
         label="US tariff on Chinese goods", zorder=5, clip_on=False)
ax1.plot(x_t, china_tariff, color=C_CN, linewidth=2.0, marker="s", markersize=4.5,
         markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.5, markeredgecolor=C_CN,
         label="China tariff on US goods", zorder=5, clip_on=False)

# Step-annotation: show the big jumps
jump_annotations = [
    (3, 12.0, "Jul 2018\nLists 1&2", C_US),
    (4, 18.3, "May 2019\nList 3 ⇧25%", C_US),
    (14, 25.4, "May 2024\nBiden hike", C_US),
]
for jx, jy, jtxt, jc in jump_annotations:
    ax1.annotate(jtxt, xy=(jx, jy), xytext=(jx + 0.6, jy + 5.5),
                fontsize=6.5, color=jc, ha="left", fontweight="bold",
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=jc, lw=1.0, connectionstyle="arc3,rad=0.15"),
                zorder=8)

ax1.set_ylabel("Effective tariff rate (%)", fontsize=9.5)
ax1.set_title("A   Tariff Escalation & Key Policy Events (2017–2024)", loc="left",
              fontweight="bold", pad=10)
ax1.set_xticks(x_t)
ax1.set_xticklabels(tariff_periods, fontsize=7)
ax1.set_ylim(0, 36)
ax1.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(5))
ax1.grid(True, axis="y", color=C_GRID, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax1.set_xlim(-0.5, 14.8)

# Policy event markers along bottom
for i, (edate, elabel, ecat) in enumerate(events_data):
    ex = date_to_idx(edate)
    color_map = {"tariff": C_TARIFF_EVENT, "investigation": C_INVESTIGATION,
                 "deal": C_DEAL, "review": C_REVIEW}
    ec = color_map.get(ecat, "#555555")
    marker_map = {"tariff": "v", "investigation": "D", "deal": "s", "review": "o"}
    em = marker_map.get(ecat, "o")

    # Stagger y positions to avoid overlap
    y_base = -2.5
    stagger = (i % 3) * 2.5

    ax1.plot(ex, y_base - stagger, marker=em, color=ec, markersize=7, zorder=9,
             markeredgewidth=0.8, markeredgecolor="white", clip_on=False)
    ax1.axvline(x=ex, ymin=0.02, ymax=0.96, color=ec, linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.5,
                linestyle="--", zorder=1)
    ax1.annotate(elabel, xy=(ex, y_base - stagger), xytext=(ex, y_base - stagger - 1.8),
                fontsize=5.8, color=ec, ha="center", va="top", zorder=9,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.2", facecolor="white", edgecolor=ec,
                         alpha=0.9, linewidth=0.5))

# Phase shading
shade_periods = [
    (-0.5, date_to_idx("2018-07-01"), "Pre-trade war"),
    (date_to_idx("2020-01-01"), date_to_idx("2021-01-01"), "Phase One"),
]
for x0, x1, label in shade_periods:
    ax1.axvspan(x0, x1, alpha=0.05, color="gray", zorder=0)
    ax1.annotate(label, xy=((x0+x1)/2, 33), fontsize=6.5, color="#777777",
                ha="center", style="italic")

# Legend
legend_elements1 = [
    Line2D([0], [0], color=C_US, linewidth=2, marker="o", markersize=4,
           markerfacecolor="white", markeredgecolor=C_US, label="US tariff on Chinese goods"),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=C_CN, linewidth=2, marker="s", markersize=4,
           markerfacecolor="white", markeredgecolor=C_CN, label="China tariff on US goods"),
]
legend_elements2 = [
    Line2D([0], [0], marker="D", color="w", markerfacecolor=C_INVESTIGATION, markersize=6, label="Investigation"),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker="v", color="w", markerfacecolor=C_TARIFF_EVENT, markersize=6, label="Tariff action"),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker="s", color="w", markerfacecolor=C_DEAL, markersize=6, label="Trade deal"),
    Line2D([0], [0], marker="o", color="w", markerfacecolor=C_REVIEW, markersize=6, label="Policy review"),
]
leg1 = ax1.legend(handles=legend_elements1, loc="upper left", frameon=True,
                  framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="#cccccc", borderpad=0.5, fontsize=7)
ax1.add_artist(leg1)
ax1.legend(handles=legend_elements2, loc="upper right", frameon=True,
           framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="#cccccc", borderpad=0.5, fontsize=6.5,
           title="Policy event markers", title_fontsize=6.5)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PANEL B: Supply Chain Diversion
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1])

ax2.plot(years_annual, china_sc, color=C_CN, linewidth=2.2, marker="o", markersize=6,
         markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.8, markeredgecolor=C_CN,
         label="China", zorder=5)
ax2.plot(years_annual, vietnam_sc, color=C_VN, linewidth=2.2, marker="s", markersize=6,
         markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.8, markeredgecolor=C_VN,
         label="Vietnam", zorder=5)
ax2.plot(years_annual, india_sc, color=C_IN, linewidth=2.2, marker="^", markersize=6,
         markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.8, markeredgecolor=C_IN,
         label="India", zorder=5)

# Net change arrows
ax2.annotate("−8.6 pp", xy=(2024, 12.8), xytext=(2024.3, 14.5),
            fontsize=7.5, color=C_CN, ha="left", fontweight="bold",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=C_CN, lw=1.2), zorder=6)
ax2.annotate("+2.8 pp", xy=(2024, 4.9), xytext=(2024.3, 5.8),
            fontsize=7.5, color=C_VN, ha="left", fontweight="bold",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=C_VN, lw=1.2), zorder=6)
ax2.annotate("+1.3 pp", xy=(2024, 3.4), xytext=(2024.3, 4.2),
            fontsize=7.5, color=C_IN, ha="left", fontweight="bold",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=C_IN, lw=1.2), zorder=6)

# Tariff start reference line
ax2.axvline(x=2018, color="#555555", linewidth=0.7, linestyle="--", alpha=0.4, zorder=1)
ax2.annotate("Tariffs\nbegin\n(2018)", xy=(2018, 22), fontsize=6.5, color="#666666",
            ha="center", va="top", style="italic")

# COVID marker
ax2.annotate("COVID-19\npandemic", xy=(2020, 10), fontsize=6.5, color="#888888",
            ha="center", style="italic")

ax2.set_ylabel("Share of total US goods imports (%)", fontsize=9.5)
ax2.set_title("B   Supply Chain Diversion: China's Declining Share vs. Rising Vietnam & India",
              loc="left", fontweight="bold", pad=10)
ax2.set_xticks(years_annual)
ax2.set_xlim(2015.3, 2024.7)
ax2.set_ylim(0, 24)
ax2.grid(True, axis="y", color=C_GRID, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax2.legend(loc="upper right", frameon=True, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="#cccccc",
           fancybox=False, borderpad=0.5, ncol=3, fontsize=7.5)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PANEL C: Bilateral Trade Volume
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2])

# Import bars
bar_w = 0.55
bars_import = ax3.bar(years_annual, us_imports, bar_w, color=C_BAR_IMPORT, alpha=0.75,
                      label="US imports from China", zorder=2, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.3)
# Export bars (total height, showing stacked effect)
bars_export = ax3.bar(years_annual, us_exports, bar_w, bottom=us_imports, color=C_BAR_EXPORT,
                      alpha=0.85, label="US exports to China", zorder=2, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.3)

# Total bilateral trade line overlay
ax3.plot(years_annual, total_bilat, color="#222222", linewidth=2.5, marker="D", markersize=6,
         markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.8, markeredgecolor="#222222",
         label="Total bilateral trade", zorder=5)

# Total value labels
for yr, tot in zip(years_annual, total_bilat):
    ax3.annotate(f"${tot:.0f}B", xy=(yr, tot), xytext=(yr, tot + 18),
                fontsize=6.5, ha="center", color="#222222", fontweight="bold", zorder=6)

# Phase One Deal reference
ax3.axvline(x=2020, color=C_DEAL, linewidth=0.8, linestyle="--", alpha=0.5, zorder=1)
ax3.annotate("Phase One\nDeal", xy=(2020, 760), fontsize=6.5, color=C_DEAL,
            ha="center", style="italic")

ax3.set_ylabel("Trade volume (billion USD)", fontsize=9.5)
ax3.set_title("C   US–China Bilateral Trade Volume (Stacked: Imports + Exports)",
              loc="left", fontweight="bold", pad=10)
ax3.set_xticks(years_annual)
ax3.set_xlim(2015.3, 2024.7)
ax3.set_ylim(0, 800)
ax3.grid(True, axis="y", color=C_GRID, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax3.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=True, framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="#cccccc",
           fancybox=False, borderpad=0.5, fontsize=7.5)

# ── Global elements ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig.suptitle("The US–China Trade War: Tariff Escalation, Trade Volume Shifts, and Supply Chain Diversion (2016–2024)",
             fontsize=15, fontweight="bold", x=0.09, ha="left", y=0.99)

fig.text(0.09, 0.01, "Sources: PIIE, US Census Bureau, USTR. Tariff rates are trade-weighted averages. 2024 trade data are estimates; tariff data through H1 2024 only. Supply chain shares may not sum to 100% due to rounding.",
         fontsize=6.2, color="#999999", style="italic")

plt.savefig("/app/output/result.png", dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor="white",
            edgecolor="none")
print("Chart saved successfully.")

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch
from datetime import datetime
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# ── Data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
tariff_periods = ["2017\nH1","2017\nH2","2018\nH1","2018\nH2","2019\nH1","2019\nH2",
                  "2020\nH1","2020\nH2","2021\nH1","2021\nH2","2022\nH1","2022\nH2",
                  "2023\nH1","2023\nH2","2024\nH1"]
us_tariff    = [3.1, 3.1, 3.8, 12.0, 18.3, 21.0, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 19.3, 25.4]
china_tariff = [8.0, 8.0, 8.0, 16.5, 20.7, 21.8, 20.9, 20.9, 20.9, 20.9, 21.1, 21.1, 21.2, 21.2, 23.1]

years_annual = np.array([2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024])
us_exports   = np.array([115.6, 129.9, 120.3, 106.4, 124.5, 151.1, 153.8, 147.8, 138.2])
us_imports   = np.array([462.6, 505.5, 539.5, 452.2, 435.4, 506.4, 536.8, 427.2, 401.5])
total_bilat  = np.array([578.2, 635.4, 659.8, 558.6, 559.9, 657.5, 690.6, 575.0, 539.7])

china_sc   = [21.4, 21.6, 21.2, 18.1, 18.6, 17.9, 16.5, 13.9, 12.8]
vietnam_sc = [2.1, 2.2, 2.6, 2.9, 3.4, 3.7, 3.9, 4.5, 4.9]
india_sc   = [2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.3, 2.7, 2.8, 3.1, 3.4]

# Policy events — simplified labels
events_data = [
    ("2017-08-14", "Section 301\nInvestigation\ninitiated", "investigation"),
    ("2018-07-06", "List 1: 25% on\n$34B goods", "tariff"),
    ("2018-09-24", "List 3: 10% on\n$200B goods", "tariff"),
    ("2019-05-10", "List 3 raised\nto 25%", "tariff"),
    ("2019-09-01", "List 4A: 15% on\n$112B goods", "tariff"),
    ("2020-01-15", "Phase One\nDeal Signed", "deal"),
    ("2021-10-04", "USTR tariff\nreview framework", "review"),
    ("2022-06-20", "Selective tariff\nexclusions review", "review"),
    ("2024-05-14", "Biden: EVs 100%,\nsemiconductors 50%", "tariff"),
]

# ── Color palette ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C_US     = "#1b3a5c"
C_CN     = "#c44e52"
C_VN     = "#dd8452"
C_IN     = "#55a868"
C_GRID   = "#d8d8d8"
C_BG     = "#fcfcfc"
C_TARIFF_EVENT = "#c44e52"
C_INVESTIGATION = "#8e6aaf"
C_DEAL   = "#3a9a5c"
C_REVIEW = "#4c9eb5"
C_BAR_EXPORT = "#3b6da8"
C_BAR_IMPORT = "#c44e52"

def date_to_idx(d):
    ref = datetime(2017, 1, 1)
    tgt = datetime.strptime(d, "%Y-%m-%d")
    days = (tgt - ref).days
    half_years = days / 182.625
    return half_years

# ── Figure ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "serif",
    "font.size": 9,
    "axes.titlesize": 11.5,
    "axes.labelsize": 9.5,
    "axes.linewidth": 0.6,
    "xtick.labelsize": 7.5,
    "ytick.labelsize": 7.5,
    "legend.fontsize": 7,
    "figure.facecolor": "white",
    "axes.facecolor": C_BG,
    "grid.alpha": 0.35,
})

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12.5, 14.5), dpi=200)
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 1, hspace=0.5, left=0.09, right=0.94, top=0.93, bottom=0.04)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PANEL A: Tariff Escalation with Policy Events
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0])
x_t = np.arange(len(tariff_periods))

# Fill between to highlight escalation gap
ax1.fill_between(x_t, us_tariff, china_tariff, where=np.array(china_tariff) >= np.array(us_tariff),
                 color=C_CN, alpha=0.06, zorder=1)
ax1.fill_between(x_t, china_tariff, us_tariff, where=np.array(us_tariff) > np.array(china_tariff),
                 color=C_US, alpha=0.06, zorder=1)

# Tariff lines
ax1.plot(x_t, us_tariff, color=C_US, linewidth=2.0, marker="o", markersize=4.5,
         markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.5, markeredgecolor=C_US,
         label="US tariff on Chinese goods", zorder=5, clip_on=False)
ax1.plot(x_t, china_tariff, color=C_CN, linewidth=2.0, marker="s", markersize=4.5,
         markerfacecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1.5, markeredgecolor=C_CN,
         label="China tariff on US goods", zorder=5, clip_on=False)

# Step-annotation: show the big jumps
jump_annotations = [
    (3, 12.0, "Jul 2018\nLists 1&2", C_US),
    (4, 18.3, "May 2019\nList 3 ⇧25%", C_US),
    (14, 25.4, "May 2024\nBiden hike", C_US),
]
for jx, jy, jtxt, jc in jump_annotations:
    ax1.annotate(jtxt, xy=(jx, jy), xytext=(jx + 0.6, jy + 5.5),
                fontsize=6.5, color=jc, ha="left", fontweight="bold",
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=jc, lw=1.0, connectionstyle="arc3,rad=0.15"),
                zorder=8)

ax1.set_ylabel("Effective tariff rate (%)", fontsize=9.5)
ax1.set_title("A   Tariff Escalation & Key Policy Events (2017–2024)", loc="left",
              fontweight="bold", pad=10)
ax1.set_xticks(x_t)
ax1.set_xticklabels(tariff_periods, fontsize=7)
ax1.set_ylim(0, 36)
ax1.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(5))
ax1.grid(True, axis="y", color=C_GRID, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax1.set_xlim(-0.5, 14.8)

# Policy event markers along bottom
for i, (edate, elabel, ecat) in enumerate(events_data):
    ex = date_to_idx(edate)
    color_map = {"tariff": C_TARIFF_EVENT, "investigation": C_INVESTIGATION,
